Strips XML/illustration fragments,\nrejects verbatim duplicates via SHA-256 fingerprint.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport hashlib\nimport re\nfrom typing import Optional\n\n# Singleton seen-fingerprints set — survives across calls in-process\n_SEEN: set[str] = set()\n\n# Patterns to strip from goal text before fingerprinting\n_XML_RE = re.compile(r'<.*?>', re.DOTALL)\n_ASCII_ART_RE = re.compile(r'^[\\s\\-_=|/\\\\]{4,}$', re.MULTILINE)\n\n\ndef _fingerprint(text: str) -> str:\n    """SHA-256 of normalized text.\"\"\"\n    normalized = text.strip().lower()\n    return hashlib.sha256(normalized.encode(\"utf-8\")).hexdigest()\n\n\ndef sanitize_and_dedupe(\n    raw_goal: str,\n    *,\n    reset: bool = False,\n) -> Optional[str]:\n    \"\"\"Return cleaned goal text, or None if duplicate/rejected.\n\n    Args:\n        raw_goal: The incoming goal text.\n        reset: If True, clear the seen-set (use in tests).\n    \"\"\"\n    if reset:\n        _SEEN.clear()\n\n    # Step 1: strip XML fragments and ASCII art lines\n    cleaned = _XML_RE.sub('', raw_goal)\n    cleaned = _ASCII_ART_RE.sub('', cleaned)\n    cleaned = cleaned.strip()\n\n    # Step 2: reject empty / too-short after stripping\n    if len(cleaned) < 10:\n        return None\n\n    # Step 3: fingerprint dedup\n    fp = _fingerprint(cleaned)\n    if fp in _SEEN:\n        return None  # duplicate — reject silently\n    _SEEN.add(fp)\n\n    return cleaned\n\n\ndef seen_count() -> int:\n    \"\"\"Number of unique fingerprints stored.\"\"\"\n    return len(_SEEN)"}

### [INSIGHT] The system exhibits a **completion-forgetting loop**: the...
- **Timestamp**: 9/16/2026, 10:00:59 AM
- **Logseq Link**: [[2026-09-16]]
- **Details**:
  The system exhibits a **completion-forgetting loop**: the same three goals (HelloGitHub scraper ×4, sanitizer ×3) keep being "completed" because completion state isn't persisting into the goal scheduler's read path — it writes to volatile memory but the queue reads a stale snapshot, re-queueing already-done work. The ASCII-art payloads corrupting goal descriptions prove output-stream artifacts are being ingested as goal text, meaning the deduplication layer was built *around* the bug instead of *into* the persistence layer where it belongs. Every "fix" generates new goals rather than patching the completion gate itself.

  The frequency signature is unmistakable: every recurring failure — write_file missing `path`, search_code missing pattern, shell_exec missing command, list_files failing entirely — is the same single disease. The agent emits tool calls with empty or truncated argument payloads, the validator correctly rejects them, and each rejection tombstone re-enters the goal queue as a fresh goal, perpetuating the recon loop. The cure is not post-hoc quarantine but pre-flight argument validation at emission time, rejecting any call whose required arguments are absent before it ever reaches the executor — breaking the self-reinforcing loop at its source.
